detail.longDescription:
If you are wondering what happened to https://amadaluzia.is-a.dev, I purposely took it down. This comes as a result of not really wanting the "is-a.dev" domain anymore, as I don't really feel like I'm in the GitHub community which is kind of what the domain suggests in my view. I do not really think the "vercel.dev" or something else is really something I fancy either. I would much rather show my support of places like Codeberg than Vercel or Cloudflare, and I want to do that by demonstrating my own tooling rather than a JS framework which might not even work for some folk.

To elaborate on this, I have the separate and currently unmaintained <https://amadaluzia.codeberg.page> which was made in glerc back when it wasn't archived. However, things have changed a lot since then, and it could really use some reconstruction. Although I said glerc is archived, I did not say that glerc was *dead*, as it has a successor project.

scaff is what I want to call a continuation of glerc that aims to separate itself from its werc-based origins. It is also based on work I did rewriting glerc to v2 based on many changes that @sewn@treehouse.systems recommended. It is also a structural rewrite of glerc itself, made as a library devoid of any I/O operations, with a CLI tool filling in that gap alongside it. There's a lot of issues to iron out still but it's probably my favourite project I have worked on thus far.

<https://codeberg.org/foxworks/scaff>

With scaff, I feel like I can bring my old codeberg.page back from the dead, so keep an eye on it. I also plan to bring back some of my old blog posts from my old page onto the new page, which should hopefully not cause any issues. The good part is that I can fix them if I do come across them, and I can get it fixed on my own terms rather than asking in a support channel and either getting bullshit for an answer or never getting a response.

#codeberg #webdev #programming #golang #software #opensource
